$comment: WHERE the bridge reads each protocol schema's payload (or builds it, for a *Params schema): named functions of bridge/src, or a whole file when the file reads nothing else. Consumed by the coverage truth guard (test/coverage-truth.test.ts, V3): inside these sites a field name is THAT schema's field, so a field the PROMISED version's coverage manifest declares gap or ignored and that a site touches is a false declaration — unless the access is ADMITTED (a gap whose knownReaders token is exactly `<receiver>.<field>` in that file) or EXCEPTED here. An exception names ONE concrete access: the field, the site (file + function) and the receivers it is read through (the text before `.field`, without casts or `?.`). Without `branch` it says those receivers are another object (a homonym): refused when one of them carries a HANDLED field of the schema anywhere in the group (that receiver is the payload, aliases included). With `branch` ({receiver, field}) it says the field is read only on branches of that discriminant the schema never takes: the schema's own literal for it is read from the VENDORED schema (never declared here), and every access must be provably unreachable when the discriminant equals it (under a test that excludes it, or after `if (…R.field === own…) return`). The guard also refuses a schema the bridge reads (a handled field) that is neither scoped here nor listed in `unscoped` with why; `unscoped` can only shrink (FROZEN_UNSCOPED in the test). `emissionStreams` ties a coverage schema that describes agent `data` to its stream in the emission registry (protocol/openclaw/emissions/<version>.json), whose classification it must not contradict.

exceptions.why: projectChat reads agentId on its DELTA branch only (the base a delta appends to); a final returns before it
projectChat reads agentId on its DELTA branch only (the base a delta appends to); an aborted frame returns before it
projectChat reads agentId on its DELTA branch only (the base a delta appends to); an error frame returns before it
projectChat reads agentId on its DELTA branch only (the base a delta appends to); a status frame returns before it
handleChat reads errorMessage for state error only: the aborted branch finalizes and returns before the read (the gap: an abort's cancellation reason is dropped)
`frame.type` at this site is the response ENVELOPE's discriminant (res / event), read before the hello-ok payload; the payload's own `type` is not read
`label` at this site is a thinking level's label (`o.label` of thinkingLevels), not the session's own label
`config.kind` at this site is the bridge's own instance configuration (openclaw / hermes), not an agent row's kind
`.sessionKey` at this site is the job OWNER's (owner.sessionKey, kept as ownerSessionKey), not the job's own sessionKey
readOpenClawApprovalCheck reads an exec or plugin presentation's agent only: a system-agent approval is raised by the gateway's own system agent, whatever the chat, and its agent is never compared

unscoped.ChatSendParams: built inline in performSendComposed (server.ts), a route function whose object literals carry many payloads at once: no site isolates this schema until its builder is a function of its own
unscoped.SessionsPatchParams: built inline in several server.ts route functions (applySessionSettings, performSendComposed) that write other payloads too: no site isolates this schema until its builder is a function of its own
unscoped.CronGetParams: built inline in performOpenClawCronManage (server.ts), which builds every cron.* request: no site isolates one schema until each builder is a function of its own
unscoped.CronListParams: built inline in fetchCronJobs (server.ts), which also reads the cron.list reply: no site isolates the params until the builder is a function of its own

unscoped.CronUpdateParams: built inline in performOpenClawCronManage (server.ts), which builds every cron.* request: no site isolates one schema until each builder is a function of its own
unscoped.ModelsListParams: built from modelsQuery's decision inside the models cache (models-roster.ts askModels), whose names are the catalogue's too: no site isolates the params until the builder is a function of its own
unscoped.TalkClientCreateResult: read inline in the talk routes of createBridgeServer (server.ts), the bridge's whole HTTP surface: no site isolates this schema until its reader is a function of its own
